title: The Vector of the Rust Belt
premise: Tamsin Delacroix, an insurance investigator who faked his own identity to survive the fall of the Belt colonies, is sent to examine the Meridian, a freighter returned from deep space with a crew grown decades younger. Aboard he finds a recording from a future that no longer exists, carrying coordinates and a message that could force the Earth Combine and the Belt Compact to the negotiating table. Hunted by both governments and by the Meridian's sole surviving officer, who wants the message destroyed to protect her own future, Tamsin must choose between staying invisible and becoming the courier history needs. He delivers the message at the cost of his anonymity, his ship, and nearly his life, ending the war by exposing that both sides were being manipulated by the same arms cartel — and finally earning a name, and a home, he can keep.
about_author: Oscar Ashgrove is a former logistics auditor who spent a decade writing risk assessments for orbital shipping firms before turning to fiction. He writes near-future science fiction about ordinary people caught in machinery far larger than themselves.

chapters.title: Actuarial Grace
chapters.summary: Tamsin Delacroix, POV. Investigating a cargo loader's 'impossible' death in Ceres dock, Tamsin quietly falsifies his findings to protect a dockworker, revealing his habit of small mercies and his fear of exposure. Emotional beat: weary competence masking a man who has erased his own past to survive.

chapters.title: The Meridian Comes Home
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. The freighter Meridian docks unbidden after eleven years missing; its nine-person crew has aged backward, now younger than their service photos. Tamsin is assigned the claim because no one else will touch it. Emotional beat: dread and fascination as the impossible lands in his lap.

chapters.title: Younger Than Her File
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. He interviews First Officer Ilsa Reyes, physically twenty-six though her records say forty. She is evasive, hostile, and terrified of something other than the anomaly. Emotional beat: two guarded people recognizing each other's masks.

chapters.title: Black Box, Redacted
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. The Meridian's flight recorder has been wiped — not by the company, not by either navy. Someone aboard did it, or someone boarded before docking. Emotional beat: the case shifts from mystery to conspiracy, and Tamsin realizes he is being watched.

chapters.title: Three Years Invisible
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV, with flashback to the fall of the Belt colonies. We learn how he bought a dead man's identity after his own name landed on a Combine purge list, and why he hauls cargo through contested orbits: invisibility is the only country he can live in. Emotional beat: grief for the self he burned.

chapters.title: The Message in the Hold
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Reyes, alternating POV. Searching the Meridian's sealed hold, they find a quantum-locked data core that predates the ship's departure — a message addressed to no one and everyone, timestamped from a future that hasn't happened. Emotional beat: awe curdling into fear of what it demands.

chapters.title: Everyone Wants the Courier
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Combine agents and Compact sympathizers both offer him protection and threats within hours of the core's discovery. His handler at the insurance syndicate reveals she has known his real name for years. Emotional beat: the floor of invisibility drops away.

chapters.title: What Reyes Buried
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. She confesses the crew found the core outbound, read it, and voted to erase it — because the message names the cartel that armed both sides, and names the Meridian's own owners as partners. She alone voted to keep it. Emotional beat: guilt as a kind of gravity.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Survival
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. He runs the numbers like an investigator: delivering the core saves millions and kills him; selling it makes him rich and damns the Belt; destroying it restores his invisibility. Emotional beat: the cold clarity of a man who has always priced his own life cheaply.

chapters.title: Dock Nine Burn
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Reyes, POV. Assassins hit the Meridian; the remaining crew scatter or die, and Tamsin and Reyes escape with the core on a battered tug through contested orbits. Emotional beat: adrenaline and the first flicker of trust between them.

chapters.title: Contested Space
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Running dark between patrol lines, Tamsin teaches Reyes the smuggler's craft of being no one, and she begins teaching him the mathematics behind the core's message. Emotional beat: intimacy built from shared danger and shared secrets.

chapters.title: The Cartel's Face
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. Decoding deeper, she finds the message includes evidence that the cartel's director is a revered Combine admiral — the war's supposed peacemaker. Emotional beat: disillusionment; the enemy was never the other side.

chapters.title: A Price on Both Heads
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Bounty notices circulate with his real name — the one he buried — and Reyes's photo. His old syndicate disavows him. Emotional beat: the last door to his old life closes, and to his surprise he feels lighter.

chapters.title: The Belt That Raised Me
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. They shelter in a refugee habitat he helped flee years ago; people who remember his real name hide him anyway, asking nothing. Emotional beat: belonging offered freely for the first time, and the ache of having refused it so long.

chapters.title: Reyes's Bargain
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. A cartel fixer offers Reyes her old life, her aged-forward future restored, if she hands over the core. She nearly takes it. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh, and the moment she refuses it.

chapters.title: Intercept at Ganymede
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Reyes, POV. A Combine cruiser corners them; the captain, secretly anti-cartel, offers to carry the core to the armistice talks — but Tamsin must testify under his real name, on record, forever. Emotional beat: the choice he has dodged for three years arrives with a deadline.

chapters.title: The Long Silence
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Waiting out a solar storm, Tamsin records his testimony and finally says his true name aloud. Reyes tells him who she was before the Meridian aged her backward — a mother, a daughter, all of it unwritten now. Emotional beat: mourning and release.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Airlock
chapters.summary: Reyes, POV. The cruiser's executive officer is cartel; Reyes is taken and the core seized, but she triggers a dead-man broadcast of its index. Emotional beat: terror, then cold resolve as she turns her captivity into a weapon.

chapters.title: Everything He Was
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Tamsin trades his testimony — his name, his history, his immunity — to the armistice delegates in exchange for a strike on the cartel's flagship where the core and Reyes are held. Emotional beat: a man spending the last of his anonymity like his final coin.

chapters.title: The Vector
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Boarding action amid the armistice summit's orbit; Tamsin recovers the core and broadcasts the message fleet-wide — the cartel's ledger, the admiral's signature, the future's warning. Emotional beat: climax, sacrifice, and the strange calm of being fully seen.

chapters.title: After the Message
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Reyes, POV. The cartel collapses, ceasefire talks resume on honest footing, and the admiral falls. Tamsin, publicly named, finds he cannot go back to being no one — and no longer wants to. Emotional beat: exhaustion, relief, the vertigo of a future with no mask.

chapters.title: A Name Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Tamsin, POV. Months later, Tamsin runs a small salvage outfit out of the refugee habitat, Reyes at his side, the Meridian's crew rebuilding lives out of order. He signs his real name to a shipping manifest and watches it mean something. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — belonging earned, survival paid for, power refused.
